### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

### Motivation

In [dsa_backend.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py), when the KV cache is stored in FP8 but `flashmla_sparse` is used to compute sparse attention in BF16, the prefix path currently dequantizes the entire flattened KV sequence:

```python
# bf16 path (dsa_impl == "flashmla_sparse").
if _has_prefix:
    page_table_1_flattened = (
        self.forward_metadata.page_table_1_flattened
    )
    assert page_table_1_flattened is not None
    kv_cache = dequantize_k_cache_paged(
        kv_cache, page_table_1_flattened
    )
else:
    kv_cache = _cat([k, k_rope], dim=-1)
```

However, DSA only attends to the top-k KV tokens selected for each query token. Therefore, especially for long contexts, dequantizing the whole sequence may introduce unnecessary dequantization work, memory traffic, and BF16 staging memory.

There is another consideration for sparse prefill. A prefill chunk contains multiple query tokens, and their top-k selections may have many overlapping KV positions. A naive per-query selective dequantization implementation could therefore dequantize the same KV position multiple times.

### Feature request

Could we add an optimized BF16 path that only dequantizes the required KV positions?

For example, it could construct the union of the top-k positions selected by all query tokens in the prefill chunk, dequantize each unique KV position once into a compact BF16 buffer, and remap the top-k indices to this compact buffer.

Since deduplication and index remapping also introduce overhead, a heuristic or fallback to the current full-sequence dequantization path may be needed when selective dequantization is not beneficial.

The goal is to keep the memory benefit of FP8 KV-cache storage while still performing sparse attention computation in BF16, without paying the cost of dequantizing the whole sequence.

This is different from the native FP8 `flashmla_sparse_q8` path, because the requested path still performs the attention computation in BF16.

Would this be feasible while maintaining good end-to-end sparse prefill performance?

### Related resources

- \#11655 introduced the current FP8-to-BF16 paged dequantization path.
- \#30514 added native FP8 sparse prefill, which avoids the BF16 staging path but uses FP8 attention computation.
title: [Feature] Selective FP8 KV dequantization for BF16 DSA sparse prefill
